extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: TextVQA is a dataset containing 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reasoning about text in images to answer. Images are sourced from Open Images v3 dataset from categories that tend to contain text (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard). Each question-image pair has 10 ground truth answers provided by humans. The dataset is designed to facilitate progress on VQA models that can read and reason about text in images.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach (Facebook AI Research, Georgia Institute of Technology)
extraction.citeAs: Singh, A., Natarajan, V., Shah, M., Jiang, Y., Chen, X., Batra, D., Parikh, D., & Rohrbach, M. (2019). Towards VQA Models That Can Read. arXiv:1904.08920v2.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected through a three-stage crowdsourcing pipeline. In the first stage, annotators identified and removed images without text. In the second stage, annotators provided 1-2 questions per image requiring reading text in the image to answer. In the third stage, 10 answers were collected per question. Images were sourced from Open Images v3 dataset, selecting categories likely to contain text using OCR-based category weighting.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In some cases, the OCR system was unable to detect text, resulting in 0 tokens for approximately 1,500 images. These images were manually verified to actually contain text. Additionally, questions where a majority of workers marked flags (no text in image, not a question, answering doesn't require reading text, unanswerable) were removed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from Open Images v3 dataset, selecting categories that tend to contain text (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard). 100 random images per category were sampled, and the Rosetta OCR system was run to compute average OCR boxes per category, which were used as sampling weights.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images from Open Images v3 training set were used for TextVQA training and validation sets, while images from Open Images v3 test set were used for the TextVQA test set. Categories were weighted by average number of OCR boxes detected by Rosetta. The dataset was split into train (34,602), validation (5,000), and test (5,734) with no image overlap between sets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A three-stage pipeline was used: (1) Annotators flagged images without text; flagged images and noisy annotator data were filtered out, resulting in 28,408 images. (2) Questions were collected and filtered using four quality flags (no text in image, not a question, answering doesn't require reading text, unanswerable); questions where a majority of workers marked any flag were removed. (3) Hand-crafted questions with known correct answers were used to identify and filter out bad annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A three-stage crowdsourcing pipeline was used. Stage 1: Annotators identified images without text using a forced-choice yes/no flag. Stage 2: Annotators provided questions requiring reading text in the image to answer; a second question with a different answer was also collected per image. Stage 3: 10 answers were collected per question following instructions similar to VQA and VizWiz datasets. Annotators were given four quality flags to catch poor quality data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All 10 annotators agreed on the most common answer for 22.8% of questions, while 3 or more annotators agreed on the most common answer for 97.9% of questions. TextVQA contains 26,263 (49.2%) unique majority answers, which is much higher than VQA 2.0 (3.4%) and VizWiz (22.8%). Human accuracy was measured at 85.01% on validation and 86.79% on test.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Rosetta OCR system was used to identify text-containing image categories and to analyze OCR tokens in the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is motivated by the needs of visually impaired users, for whom up to 21% of questions asked of assistive devices involve reading and reasoning about text in images. Progress on this dataset could improve assistive technologies for visually impaired users.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The most common answer ('yes') is the majority answer for only 4.71% of the dataset. Question-only and image-only baselines achieve low accuracy (8.09% and 6.29% respectively), suggesting limited dataset bias with respect to questions and images. The model shows a bias toward predicting 'new york' for city-related questions. The dataset was collected by sighted humans rather than visually impaired users.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset was collected from sighted humans rather than visually impaired users. The OCR model fails at detecting text that is rotated, unstructured (e.g., a scribble), or partially occluded. 8.9% of TextVQA questions can only be answered by combining multiple OCR tokens, which the current model cannot handle. The effective answer space is highly diverse, making fixed answer space approaches insufficient.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of VQA models that can read and reason about text in images. The dataset is intended to benchmark progress on VQA models along directions complementary to VQA 2.0, specifically for reading and reasoning about text in natural everyday scenes.
